notes: 2025-11-20: Intro call (AE Maya) — high-level use cases: conversational support for high-value customers, automated underwriting summaries, reranking candidate answers for compliance checks.
2025-12-05: Technical deep-dive with SE (Ravi) — discussed model latency targets and multi-tenant isolation. Customer emphasized predictability over best-effort low cost.
2026-01-10: Submitted initial capacity questionnaire — asking for sustained throughput numbers, burst policies, and warm-pool strategy.

2026-01-30: Deep arch call (ff-2026-01-30-architectural-deep-dive) — Archipelago runs peak traffic cycles tied to NY market hours; typical baseline 600 reqs/min across collection of endpoints, with 3x bursts during open/close windows.
POC started 2026-02-01: 2-week sandbox using dedicated pool (4x A100 equivalent nodes), baseline targets defined.

POC acceptance criteria (customer): p95 latency <120ms for 512-token chat requests under sustained load; cold-start tail <300ms; throughput 1.8k tokens/s aggregate; no more than 1% request failures during peak bursts.
Customer asked for throughput guarantees + SLA credits for missed p95 targets. Procurement pushed back on vague burst pricing — wants committed reserved GPUs + clear overage bands.
Reserved GPU planning: customer prefers committed pool for core business flows (customer-facing chat + underwriting) and an auto-scale/burst pool for non-critical batch jobs.

Scale-up policy discussed: add nodes when queue depth > 40 for 30s or when sustained CPU/GPU utilization > 80% for 60s. They prefer fast scale-up (seconds) but cautious about noisy autoscaling causing thrashing.
Scale-down policy discussed: cool-down 5 minutes after utilization drops below 30% to avoid repeated scale toggles; maintain a minimum warm pool of 10% reserved nodes to reduce cold-starts.
Warm pools: customer wants warm KV-cache priming for top 500 prefixes and a 10% warm capacity target to handle sudden spikes; asked for metrics on warm pool memory usage and cost delta.
Queueing behavior: acceptable max queue wait = 200ms for high-priority customer flows; background batch requests can queue up to 10s before auto-fallover to cheaper quantized model.
Fallbacks: automatic fallback to a quantized 8-bit variant for non-critical responses when dominant pool is saturated. For high-value customer chats, route to backup region with reserved capacity.
Operational controls: need per-route SLOs, token-level cost breakdowns, and alerting on p95 regressions. Wants automated rollbacks if SLO breaches increase by >20% in 24h.
Monitoring/tracing: request OpenTelemetry-compatible traces forwarded to Archipelago's Splunk instance + Redwood console metrics.
Security/compliance: legal requires written SOC2 + ISO27001 evidence, KMS integration details, and audit log retention policy for 7 years for regulatory audits.
Negotiation topics: SLA credit formula (tiered by minutes of breach), reserved capacity commitment term (12 vs 36 months), and overage pricing for burst capacity.
Current POC observations (2026-02-15): p95 stable at ~110ms under baseline; during synthetic 3x burst test saw queueing spikes and one node OOM — SE investigating autoscaling ramp parameter.

Action items from 2026-02-20: SE to tune scale-up threshold to lower queue-depth trigger; infra to provide list of recommended GPU SKUs and estimated per-node throughput; legal to prepare draft SLA template.
Procurement timeline: internal procurement review scheduled for 2026-05; target contract signature 2026-06 contingent on final SLA and reserved SKU pricing.
Quote requests: asked for two proposal options — (A) committed 8-node reserved pool + 20% burstable warm pool, (B) hybrid: 4 reserved + on-demand burst with guaranteed cold-start windows.
Customer comment (SE call): "We need deterministic tail latency more than headline throughput — our users equate delay with risk."
Recent risk: EU data residency requirement was raised for a subset of accounts — may require private on-prem slice or region-locked deployment.
Next demo: show warm-pool priming and scaled burst scenario with trace-level breakdowns; propose SLA wording for p95 and availability credit bands.
Procurement blocker: finance needs CapEx vs OpEx comparison for 12/36 month reserved options; requested run-rate projection with estimated token volumes.

Longer-term asks: autoscaling knob to prefer vertical scaling (larger GPU instances) vs horizontal (add nodes) depending on model and sequence length; cost calculator for mixed-precision/quantized fallbacks.
